items.name: Regular Noetherian rings
items.statement: IsRegularRing R means R is Noetherian and every prime localization is a regular local ring; the local class uses equality of the finite spanning rank of the maximal ideal and the Krull dimension.
proofSteps: Use the existing predicates in the main theorem statements; do not silently identify a local instance with the global predicate without proving localization regularity.

items.name: Faithfully flat module
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if it is flat and I M is proper for every maximal ideal I of R.
proofSteps: Ordinary faithful flatness is distinguished from the almost Tor and detection conditions in Proposition 5.2.

items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M, AdicCompletion I M is the module of compatible elements of M/I^n M. IsAdicComplete includes separatedness and convergence of all I-adic Cauchy sequences.

items.name: Ordinary derived category
items.statement: For an abelian category C with a chosen HasDerivedCategory instance, DerivedCategory C is the localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.

items.name: Artin–Rees
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, submodule N and ideal I, there is k such that for all n≥k, I^n M∩N=I^(n−k)(I^k M∩N).
proofSteps: Read the actual statement with its finite-module and Noetherian hypotheses.

items.name: Uniform Artin–Rees lifting
items.statement: For Noetherian R, finite M, ideal I and N⊂M, there is k independent of P and the surjection φ:P→N such that every v∈N∩I^(m+k)M lifts through φ to I^m P for every m.
proofSteps: The library quantifies k before P, φ and m. This is an available stronger control lemma, not a claim that 5.3 itself is already formalized.

items.name: Krull intersection for a proper ideal
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R, finite R-module M and proper ideal I, the intersection of I^n M is zero; in particular the intersection of I^n in R is zero.
proofSteps: Use this to detect a nonzero obstruction before adjoining roots, and to force a proper ideal containing all roots of p to be impossible.

items.name: Chosen compatible roots and their almost ideal
items.statement: Fix a prime p and a nonzerodivisor t in A with specified elements t_n, t_0=t and t_(n+1)^p=t_n. The ideal m_t is generated by all t_n. Almost zero means m_t M=0; the root choices are data.
proofSteps: Use the same chosen root system throughout each transition estimate; the ideals m_t, m_g and m_(tg) are separately named.

items.name: Almost modules and adjoints
items.statement: For an almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the required flatness of m⊗_V m, form the Serre quotient by m-annihilated modules, almostification, its right adjoint (*) and left adjoint (!); for algebras use the distinct (!!) adjoint.
items.note: Field-base supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base. General reusable-base scope is in the current P0 stage; its stronger adjoint details remain a request.
proofSteps: The module adjoint and algebra adjoint must not be interchanged in the proof of faithful detection.

items.name: Almost flat and almost faithful maps modulo t
items.statement: An algebra map modulo t is almost flat when its positive Tor groups vanish in the specified almost category, and almost faithfully flat when tensor is also conservative there.
proofSteps: The 5.2 conclusion detecting ordinary A0-modules is stronger than conservativity only on almost modules and is extracted separately.

items.name: Bhatt's field-based integral perfectoid algebra
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid and t∈K° a topologically nilpotent unit with compatible p-roots and |t|=|p| in characteristic zero. An integral perfectoid K°-algebra is K°-flat, t-adically complete, satisfies A=A_*, and Frobenius A/t^(1/p)→A/t is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

uses.how: This is the star-normalized field-based convention of the paper, not every modern general integral perfectoid ring.

items.statement: Use the integral perfectoid notion of PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, allowing rings which do not contain the valuation ring of a perfectoid field; keep its comparison to Bhatt's field-based convention explicit.

items.statement: For integral perfectoid A, let A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ be the t-adic completion of the compatible-root polynomial algebra and Y=Spa(A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩[1/t],A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩).

items.name: Integral rational localization with roots
items.statement: For a rational domain in the tilt given by f_i/g, with f_i,g integral and one f_i a power of the tilted pseudouniformizer, its untilted integral ring is almost the completed root-ratio algebra from Scholze Lemma 6.4.
proofSteps: Retain the domain and invertibility hypotheses; abstract quotient, torsion-free image and star model are related by almost comparison, not equality.

items.name: Tilt approximation preserving a rational neighborhood
items.statement: For perfectoid affinoid R, f∈R, c≥0 and ε>0, there is h in the tilt with |f(x)−h♯(x)|≤|ϖ|^(1−ε) max(|f(x)|,|ϖ|^c) for all x. For ε<1 the two maxima agree.
items.note: Supplier: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma. Source Corollary 6.7 and packet proof read; the entire Lemma 6.5 proof was not independently reread.
proofSteps: Apply to T−g so the same small rational neighborhood has an equation with compatible roots; do not use additivity of sharp.

items.name: Shrinking neighborhood algebra B_l
items.statement: For l>0, B_l is O^+ on {|T−g|≤|t|^l} in the perfectoid root disc. Restrictions B_l→B_(l+1) are the direct-system maps.
proofSteps: Use the actual restriction maps to pass from local almost flatness to adjoining roots.

items.name: Completed neighborhood extension
items.statement: Set A∞ to the t-adic completion of colim_l B_l; use its star-normalization when necessary. Then T=g in A∞, giving a specified compatible p-root system of g.
proofSteps: Divisibility of T−g by every t^l and separatedness make T=g. Footnote 6 is essential: integral perfectoidness may initially hold only almost.

items.name: Almost faithful flatness of each neighborhood
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and each l>0, A/t→B_l/t is almost faithfully flat with respect to m_t.
proofSteps: Approximate T−g by a sharp element; use the completed root-relation presentation.
At root level k reduce modulo t^ε for ε=1/p^(k+1); Frobenius identifies the quotient with a free, faithful polynomial-root algebra modulo T−g.
Pass through filtered colimits and derived completion using the precise DD.1 comparisons; the source's almost category remains m_t.

items.name: Perfection of a simplicial F_p-algebra is discrete
items.statement: For a simplicial commutative F_p-algebra C, its filtered colimit along Frobenius is discrete and identifies with the perfection of π_0(C).
proofSteps: Needed for discreteness of the perfected derived relation algebra. Exact original statement and proof are an open source-closure task G2.

items.name: Root annihilation of torsion in a perfect ring
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra with compatible roots of t and tx=0, then t^(1/p^n)x=0 for every n.
proofSteps: Taking inverse Frobenius gives t^(1/p^n)x^(1/p^n)=0; multiply by x^(1−1/p^n), represented by a nonnegative power of x^(1/p^n).

items.name: Almost discreteness of the derived root presentation
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and f_1,…,f_n,g in its integral tilt, let B be the filtered colimit over r of the Koszul complexes over A[T_i^(1/p∞)] on the relations (g^(1/p^r))♯ T_i^(1/p^r)−(f_i^(1/p^r))♯. Then Kos(B;t) is almost discrete. For an admissible rational presentation, derived t-completion of B is almost its integral rational localization.
proofSteps: Reduce to the characteristic-p tilt, perfect the derived polynomial relation algebra, then use root annihilation of its t-torsion.

Recover the completed comparison from reduction modulo t via DD.1. Split the discreteness and completion clauses in the final blueprint. The source's unqualified rational notation and its admissibility interface still need matching in G2; no extra rational-domain assumption is imposed on the discreteness assertion.

items.name: Functorial almost faithful absolutely integrally closed extension
items.statement: For every integral perfectoid K°-algebra A there is a functorial extension A→B(A), almost faithfully flat modulo t, with every monic polynomial over B(A) admitting a root.
items.note: Existing node PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma read. Its statement does not explicitly give the functorial choice required here.
proofSteps: Q3 already owns the stronger p-completely faithfully flat existence theorem for general perfectoid rings. Request only the functoriality and exact field-based comparison of this source, not a second AIC construction.

items.name: Almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: For a tower of A-modules M_n, almost-pro-zero means: for every k≥0 and n≥1 there exists m≥n such that t^(1/p^k) kills the image M_m→M_n. The later index may depend on both k and n.
proofSteps: This quantifier order is the input to all inverse-limit arguments.

items.name: Tower separating two almost notions
items.statement: For a nontrivial root-valued base such as K°, let M_n=A/(t^(1/p^n)) with transition 1↦t^(1/p^n−1/p^(n+1)). These maps are injective, the tower is almost-pro-zero, and its pro-object in almost modules is nonzero.
proofSteps: For fixed k, M_m is killed by t^(1/p^k) once m≥k. For any fixed transition into M_n, a sufficiently small positive root fails to kill its image in the valuation-ring example.

items.name: Derived inverse limit of an almost-pro-zero tower
items.statement: If M_n is almost-pro-zero, every cohomology group of Rlim_n M_n is almost zero.
proofSteps: For each k the quotient tower M_n/M_n[t^(1/p^k)] is pro-zero. Apply pro-zero-roos and the short exact sequence to identify the two derived limits.
The two-term Roos complex of M_n[t^(1/p^k)] is termwise killed by t^(1/p^k). Thus each root annihilates the resulting cohomology.

items.name: Almost-pro-isomorphisms induce almost inverse-limit isomorphisms
items.statement: A morphism of coherent countable towers of A-module complexes whose cone cohomology towers are m_t-almost-pro-zero induces an almost isomorphism on derived inverse limits. This applies to the actual bounded-complex comparisons in 3.2–3.5; coherence is retained in D(Tower(Mod_A)) or an equivalent enhancement.
proofSteps: Use the functorial cone tower rather than choose unrelated cones in D(A). The exact Roos construction commutes with this cone.
Apply module-tower-milnor to its cohomology towers. Its proof handles the product of annihilators in each Milnor extension.

items.name: A-linear functors preserve almost-pro-zero
items.statement: If F:Mod_A→Mod_A is A-linear and M_n is almost-pro-zero, then F(M_n) is almost-pro-zero.
proofSteps: Factor a sufficiently late transition through M_n[t^(1/p^k)]; A-linearity makes its image under F factor through F(M_n)[t^(1/p^k)]. No exactness assumption on F is needed.

items.name: Rational annular tower
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, put A_n=O^+({|t|^n≤|g|}⊂Spa(A[1/t],A)). The transition is A_(n+c)→A_n. Theorem 4.2 first assumes g is an almost nonzerodivisor modulo each t^m.
proofSteps: The restriction direction and almost base must survive the quotient by t^m.

items.name: Pointwise almost-zero kernels
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, for every m≥0 and n≥1, ker(A/t^m→A_n/t^m) is m_t-almost zero.
proofSteps: In the root-relation model, almost regularity of g modulo t^m controls the kernel; transport through the m_t-almost comparison.

items.name: Uniform root annihilation of cokernel transitions
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, working in m_t-almost modules, for every m,k≥0 the transition coker(f_(n+c))→coker(f_n) is annihilated by g^(1/p^k) for all n, where c=p^k m.
proofSteps: Represent monomials by u^e. For e≥p^(−k), the factor t^(ce) vanishes modulo t^m.
For e<p^(−k), multiply by g^(1/p^k) and rewrite it as a base element with exponents g^(p^(−k)−e)t^((n+c)e). The shift c is independent of n.

items.name: Quantitative Riemann extension
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1, {A/t^m}_n→{A_n/t^m}_n is an almost-pro-isomorphism for the ideal generated by compatible roots of tg.
proofSteps: Combine the m_t kernel comparison and m_g cokernel estimate after explicit change of almost base.

items.name: Uniform derived tensor version
items.statement: Under Notation 4.1 and fixed m≥1, for every k≥0 set c=p^k m. For every K∈D(A/t^m), every i and every n≥1, g^(1/p^k) kills the c-step transition on the kernels and cokernels of H^i(K)→H^i(K⊗^L_(A/t^m) A⟨t^n/g⟩/t^m) in m_t-almost modules. Consequently (tg)^(1/p^k) kills those ordinary transitions, with c independent of n, K and i. For m=0 both rings modulo t^0 are zero.
items.note: The prior G4 chain-level gap is resolved at the paper-proof level by the amplitude-zero cone argument. This is not a claim that the derived tensor API is implemented.
proofSteps: Theorem 4.2(1) identifies the almost cone of each comparison with its module cokernel, naturally in n.
Theorem 4.2(2) makes g^(1/p^k) times the c-step map of those cokernels exactly zero in almost modules, for c=p^k m.
Apply uniform-tensor-cone and tensor-kernel-cokernel. This proves the stated bound without a ghost-map assumption. The general almost derived tensor implementation remains supplied by E1/P0.

items.name: Uniform estimates for Koszul homology
items.statement: For a regular sequence in A/t^m in the setup of 4.2, nonzero-degree Koszul homology of its base change to A_n/t^m forms uniformly almost-pro-zero towers. The underlying comparison applies to any finite Koszul complex, but vanishing of the source homology uses regularity.
proofSteps: Import generic Koszul construction from DD.1; specialize its derived base-change map.

items.name: Riemann extension without regularity of g
items.statement: For integral perfectoid A and g with compatible roots, the final almost-pro-isomorphism of 4.2 holds without the almost nonzerodivisor hypothesis on g modulo t^m.
proofSteps: Apply the regular universal case K°⟨T^(1/p∞)⟩ with T, derived base change T↦g, and take H^0. This does not assert the separate pointwise kernel statement for arbitrary g.

items.name: Riemann extension after limits
items.statement: Under the introductory setup, A∞→lim_n A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is almost an isomorphism with respect to roots of pg, using the reductions and limits over m of 1.6.
proofSteps: Recover completeness by the limit over m and account for derived inverse-limit terms; this is weaker information than the quantitative tower theorem.

items.name: Lifting flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: For A Noetherian and A→B, if π is a nonzerodivisor on both rings, both are π-adically complete and A/π→B/π is flat, then A→B is flat.
proofSteps: Resolve a finite A-module by finite free modules; compare tensor with Rlim of reductions.
Finite generation bounds π-power torsion, making the extra Tor tower pro-zero. Lift flatness to all π^n reductions, then use left t-exactness of Rlim.

items.name: Lifting faithful flatness from one complete reduction
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses as 5.1, faithful flatness of A/π→B/π implies faithful flatness of A→B.
proofSteps: Every maximal ideal of π-complete A contains π. Its residue field remains nonzero after tensor with B/π; use the existing faithful-flatness criterion.

items.statement: For an unramified p-torsionfree Noetherian regular local A0 of residue characteristic p, there is a faithfully flat map to a field-based integral perfectoid algebra over the completed Q_p(p^(1/p∞)).
proofSteps: Pass faithfully flatly to a complete ring with algebraically closed residue field; use Cohen presentation W(k)[[x_2,…,x_d]], adjoin compatible roots of parameters and p, and complete.

items.statement: For the same A0→A in 5.2, if M⊗_A0 A is m_p-almost zero then the ordinary A0-module M is zero.

Reduce a nonzero M to a cyclic submodule and use almost flatness; containing every root of p would put p in all powers of a proper ideal, contrary to Krull intersection.
This ordinary detection conclusion is distinct from faithfulness in the almost category.

items.name: Adic Hom comparison as a pro-isomorphism
items.statement: For Noetherian R, ideal I and finite R-modules M,N, {Hom_R(M,N)/I^n Hom_R(M,N)}→{Hom_R(M,N/I^n N)} is a pro-isomorphism.

items.name: Splitting obstruction
items.statement: For a map A→C in D(A), form its cone Q and the connecting morphism α:Q→A[1]. The unit splits if and only if α=0. For a finite injective ring extension C=B in degree zero, Q is B/A.

items.name: Reduction to complete mixed-characteristic regular local rings
items.statement: To prove the finite splitting theorem, use localization, faithful flat completion and residue-field extension to reduce the mixed-characteristic branch to a complete regular local ring with perfect residue field and a finite domain extension generically étale after some nonzero pg.
proofSteps: Prove descent of existence of a retraction via the finite obstruction module, the component/domain reductions and existence of a discriminant element. These are named unfinished inputs G5, not automatic changes of hypotheses.

items.name: Detecting a surviving finite splitting obstruction
items.statement: In the complete local finite-extension setup of 5.4, a nonzero splitting obstruction remains nonzero modulo p^m for some m≥3, and after the two almost faithful extensions there is k such that (pg)^(1/p^k) does not annihilate the resulting obstruction.
proofSteps: Use finite Hom and vanishing lim¹ to detect nonzero reduction; choose k with p²g outside the relevant annihilator power; account for the loss of one factor p in almost-flat base change.
The p²g→pg calculation must be expanded at declaration level; retain it as G5 rather than suppressing its bound.

items.name: Almost purity for finite étale perfectoid extensions
items.statement: For a perfectoid K-algebra R and finite étale R-algebra S, S is perfectoid and S° is almost finite étale and uniformly almost finitely generated over R°. Faithfulness is a separate hypothesis when a cover or almost retraction is needed.
proofSteps: Import the accepted partial node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, preserving its proof gaps.

items.name: Almost splitting of a finite generically étale cover
items.statement: For the finite injective extensions over the rational perfectoid algebras in 5.4, finite étale after inverting p, the unit is almost split with respect to m_p.
proofSteps: Almost purity plus the finite-presentation almost-purity-to-splitting lemma annihilates the extension class. Original Bhatt 2014 Lemma 2.7 and exact finite hypotheses remain G3.

items.name: Annihilation of the finite obstruction on each annulus
items.statement: For fixed m,n in the setup of 5.4, the obstruction after base change to A∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m is m_p-almost zero.
proofSteps: The rational inequality makes g invertible after p is inverted, so the chosen generic étaleness applies.

items.name: Recovering almost vanishing over A∞
items.statement: In the setup of 5.4, annular almost vanishing implies that the obstruction over A∞/p^m is m_(pg)-almost zero.
proofSteps: Apply the A∞-linear Hom functor to the tower; it becomes almost-pro-isomorphic to a constant system. Lemma 3.5 removes the lim¹ obstruction, contradicting detection.

items.name: Direct summand theorem
items.statement: For a finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular, there exists an A0-linear map B0→A0 whose composite with the unit is the identity.
proofSteps: Combine the mixed-characteristic contradiction with the separately supplied equal-characteristic cases and descent. The retraction is module-linear, not a ring homomorphism.

items.name: Perfect proper coherent cohomology over a regular local base
items.statement: For proper X→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular local, RΓ(X,O_X) is bounded with finite cohomology, hence perfect over A0. For any A0-algebra D there is a unit-compatible map from its derived scalar extension to cohomology of the ordinary base change. This map is not asserted to be an isomorphism without additional hypotheses.
items.note: Proper coherent finiteness and perfectness remain G5/G6. The comparison map to ordinary base-change cohomology suffices for 6.1; no isomorphism is needed there.
proofSteps: Request proper coherent finiteness, finite cohomological dimension, and the finite global dimension of the Noetherian regular local base.

Use cohomology-base-change-map and splitting-through-comparison for the passage to the ordinary proper scheme over each annulus. An almost-flat base-change isomorphism is not a prerequisite for this splitting step.

items.name: Generic multisection reduction
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero fraction field, a proper surjective scheme has a closed point with finite separable residue extension. Its closure gives a proper dominating scheme which becomes finite étale after inverting a suitable nonzero pg.
proofSteps: Use existence of a closed point, its integral closure in X and shrinking of the quasi-finite proper generically separable map. Splitting for the composite dominating morphism implies splitting for the original unit.

items.name: Integral global functions in the perfectoid proper case
items.statement: For proper surjective Y→Spec(A) in the corrected 6.2 setup, B=H^0(Y,O_Y) is an integral A-algebra; B[1/p] is the finite étale generic algebra, and Y maps naturally to Spec(B).
items.note: Reclassified from missing after reading declarations at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Proper.lean:138 proves integrality for every universally closed morphism with affine target; no Noetherian or surjectivity hypothesis. QuasiSeparated.lean:401 identifies sections on a global basic open with localization for qcqs opens. GammaSpecAdjunction.lean:434,458 supplies the natural affinization map. The given proper morphism is qcqs, and Y[1/p] is its basic open for the image of p. Thus B[1/p]=Γ(Y[1/p],O), finite étale by the stated hypothesis. This is a composition of existing results, not a new general theorem to re-plan. No finiteness of B over A is asserted.
proofSteps: Apply isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed to Y→Spec(A).
Apply isLocalization_basicOpen_of_qcqs to the whole qcqs scheme Y and the image of p; identify the generic fibre with that basic open.
Use Scheme.toSpecΓ and its naturality for Y→Spec(A) to obtain Y→Spec(B) over Spec(A).

items.name: Admissible blowup domination of a generic isomorphism
items.statement: Let A be p-torsionfree and p-adically complete, and X→Spec(A) proper and an isomorphism after inverting p. There is a finitely generated ideal I⊂A containing p^N for some N≥1 and a factorization Bl_I(Spec(A))→X→Spec(A). Completing this diagram p-adically gives the formal domination required in 6.2. The algebraic factorization already suffices for the integral generic-fibre map.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2; exact algebraic supplier Stacks 081T, rather than a domination theorem attributed to GR2 §15.4
items.note: The proof source for domination has been identified. Foundational flattening leaves are still G6; GR2 §15.4 is used for rational charts and integral stalks, not mis-cited as a standalone domination theorem.
proofSteps: Apply proper-modification-domination with U=D(p), a quasi-compact open of the affine qcqs base. Choose a finite list of generators for its centre and append p^N.
Each blowup chart A[I/f] is a subring of A[1/f]; p remains regular. Its p-adic completion is the chart for the completed admissible blowup.
Use the functorial completion of the algebraic diagram only if a formal version is desired. No Noetherian formal-functions or formal-GAGA theorem is invoked.

items.name: Integral generic-fiber factorization
items.statement: For mixed-characteristic perfectoid K and normalized integral perfectoid K°-algebra A, let Sη=Spa(A[1/p],A). For every finitely generated I=(f_0,…,f_r) containing p^N, the integral locally ringed space (Sη,O^+) maps over Spec(A) to Bl_I(Spec(A)). Combining this with formal-domination gives a map to any proper model whose generic fibre is the identity.
items.locator: Bhatt 6.2 footnote 8; GR2 Release 6.95, Lemma 15.4.14(i)–(ii) and Remark 15.4.25(i)–(vi), pp. 1318–1324
proofSteps: Set U_i={x: |f_j(x)|≤|f_i(x)| for all j}. Append p^N to the generator list. These rational subsets cover Sη: at a given valuation one generator has maximal value, and that value is nonzero because |p^N|>0.
The ratios f_j/f_i are bounded sections on U_i. The map A[1/f_i]→O(U_i) restricts to A[I/f_i]→O^+(U_i), using the actual blowup algebra, including its torsion relations.
The integral stalks are local: GR2 15.4.14(ii) identifies them as the inverse image of the residual valuation ring. The chart map therefore gives a locally ringed-space map into Spec(A[I/f_i]).
On U_i∩U_j the two ratios are reciprocal bounded units. Both chart maps restrict to the same localized ring map, so glue.

Compose with the algebraic domination map. Functoriality of structure-sheaf cohomology identifies A→RΓ(Y,O_Y)→RΓ(Sη,O^+) with the structural unit. Perfectoid sheafiness/acyclicity is imported; GR2 15.4.34 is not applied without its analytically Noetherian hypothesis.

The morphism Y→Spec(B) is proper: its graph into Y×_A Spec(B) is closed because Spec(B) is separated over Spec(A), and projection is a base change of the original proper map. Thus Y_C is proper over C and has identity generic fibre.
Use algebraic blowup domination and the integral generic-fibre map to split C→RΓ(Y_C,O) by perfectoid acyclicity.
Restrict scalars and compose RΓ(Y,O)→RΓ(Y_C,O)→C→A. Its composite with A→RΓ(Y,O) is the identity in the almost derived category.

items.name: Cone of an almost injective module map
items.statement: For a commutative almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the standard flatness hypothesis on m⊗V m, a V-algebra R, and an R-module map u:M→N whose kernel is almost zero, Cone(u)^a is naturally isomorphic to coker(u)^a placed in degree zero. The isomorphism is natural in commutative squares of module maps.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, expanded from Theorem 4.2(1); ordinary cochain convention H^(-1)(Cone(u))=ker(u)
proofSteps: The two-term cone has cohomology only in degrees −1 and 0. Exact almostification removes its degree −1 cohomology.
The canonical projection Cone(u)→coker(u)[0] is therefore a quasi-isomorphism after almostification; its naturality identifies the actual transition maps, not only the objects.

items.name: Uniform tensor annihilation from module cokernels
items.statement: Let u_n:M→N_n be a compatible countable tower of module maps over R, each almost injective for m. Put Q_n=coker(u_n). If a·(Q_(n+c)→Q_n)=0 in almost R-modules for all n, then for every K∈D(R), a annihilates the transition Cone(K⊗^L u_(n+c))→Cone(K⊗^L u_n) in the almost derived category. The same c works for every K and every cohomological degree.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3; explicit derivation of its same-constant assertion
proofSteps: Use the natural cone-to-cokernel equivalence before applying derived tensor. The transition multiplied by a is the zero morphism of modules, hence zero in the derived category.
Derived tensor is R-linear and exact. Almostification commutes with derived tensor under the fixed almost-base hypotheses, so K^a⊗^L Q_n^a computes the almostified tensor cone.
Neither boundedness nor flatness of K is assumed: use the K-flat derived tensor supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1. Do not replace equality of morphisms by mere vanishing of their cohomology maps.

items.name: Uniform annihilation of tensor comparison defects
items.statement: Under uniform-tensor-cone, a kills the transition maps on both ker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) and coker(H^i(K⊗^L u_n)) in almost modules, for all i, with the same shift c. For m=m_t and a=g^(1/p^k), every t^(1/p^j)g^(1/p^k) kills the corresponding ordinary transition maps. In particular (tg)^(1/p^k) works with j=k.
items.locator: Bhatt Remark 4.3, long exact cohomology sequence of the tensor cone
proofSteps: In each degree, the cokernel of H^i(u) embeds in H^i(Cone(u)), while the kernel of H^i(u) is a quotient of H^(i−1)(Cone(u)). These are natural descriptions for the transition squares.
Restrict or pass to the quotient of the zero scalar transition; no extra shift or squaring of g is needed.
A morphism which is zero after almostification has m-annihilated image. Multiply by each specified root of t to return to ordinary modules.

items.name: Countable derived limit of coherent module towers

This descends to D(Tower(Mod_R)), is exact, and computes the right derived inverse limit. The countable products are degreewise; these formulas are not asserted for arbitrary sheaf categories.

proofSteps: Use exactness of products of R-modules to preserve quasi-isomorphisms and identify product cohomology. The standard two-column Roos resolution computes the derived limit.
Strict maps of towers give commuting squares on products and thus functorial maps of cones. Totalize the two finite cone directions to compare Rlim(Cone(u_n)) with Cone(Rlim(u)).

items.name: Derived acyclicity of a pro-zero module tower
items.statement: For a countable pro-zero tower M_n of R-modules, 1−s on ∏M_n is invertible. Hence lim M_n=lim¹ M_n=0 and Rlim M_n=0. More generally, a levelwise morphism of module towers whose kernel and cokernel towers are pro-zero induces an isomorphism on derived inverse limits.
items.locator: Bhatt 3.4 proof input; Stacks 07KV, Lemmas 15.88.4 and 15.88.16; explicit product proof
proofSteps: Define ((1−s)^(-1)b)_n=Σ_(j≥n) transition_(j,n)(b_j). For each n all sufficiently late transition maps are zero, so the sum is finite at that coordinate. Telescope to verify both inverse identities.
For a levelwise pro-isomorphism, split its four-term kernel/cokernel exact sequence using its image tower. Apply exactness of the Roos functor to the two short exact sequences.
For arbitrary pro-representatives use cofinal reindexing and Stacks 15.88.4; preserve coherence when specifying a map in the derived category.

items.name: Milnor sequence for coherent module-complex towers
items.statement: For the tower-roos construction and every integer i, there is a natural short exact sequence 0→lim¹ H^(i−1)(K_n)→H^i(Rlim K_n)→lim H^i(K_n)→0. If every H^i(K_n) is m_t-almost-pro-zero, then H^i(Rlim K_n) is m_t-almost zero.
proofSteps: Take the long exact cohomology sequence of 1−s and use exact module products; its kernel and cokernel are lim and lim-one.
For each a=t^(1/p^k), the inclusion M_n[a]→M_n has pro-zero cokernel by almost-pro-zero. Its Roos comparison is an isomorphism, so a kills lim and lim-one of M_n.

Both ends of the Milnor extension are therefore almost zero. Explicitly choose b=t^(1/p^(k+1)); b² kills the middle, and t^(1/p^k)=b²·b^(p−2). This records the annihilator product that an extension requires.
This uses exact products for modules, not unproved left completeness of arbitrary sheaf-derived categories.

items.name: Flattening by an admissible blowup
items.statement: Let S be qcqs, U⊂S a quasi-compact open, X→S quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and F a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module. If F|_(X_U) is of finite presentation and flat over U, some U-admissible blowup S′→S makes its strict transform finitely presented over X×_S S′ and flat over S′. No Noetherian assumption is made.
items.locator: Stacks 0815, Theorem 38.30.7, statement and proof read; auxiliary leaves listed in G6
proofSteps: The source reduces étale locally to affine schemes and inducts on the maximum fibre dimension of Supp(F).
Its local presentation lemma 38.3.2 reduces via a finite pushforward to a smooth affine morphism with geometrically irreducible fibres.

Lemma 38.30.3 gives a finite locally free locus surjecting over the base. A chosen free submodule is universally injective by 38.10.1; its cokernel has smaller fibre-support dimension, so apply induction.
After making U schematically dense, 38.11.1 supplies finite presentation. These invoked proof leaves and the étale gluing in 38.30.6 remain explicit source-closure obligations, not assumed solved.

items.name: Flattening a finite type scheme generically of finite presentation
items.statement: For qcqs S, quasi-compact open U, and a finite type quasi-separated X→S whose restriction to U is flat and locally of finite presentation, some U-admissible blowup makes the strict transform X′ flat and finitely presented over S′.
proofSteps: Cover X by finitely many affines and find a common admissible refinement of the blowups for them (Stacks 080J, 31.35.4).
Embed each affine as a closed subscheme of a quasi-compact open V in affine space over S. Apply flattening-modification to i_*O_X on V.
Strict transform commutes with affine pushforward (31.34.4, still a supplier obligation). Finite presentation of the transformed structure sheaf then gives finite presentation of the scheme.

items.name: A flat generic isomorphism is an open immersion
items.statement: If f:X→S is separated, locally of finite type and flat, and U⊂S is retrocompact and schematically dense with f^(-1)(U)→U an isomorphism, then f is an open immersion.
proofSteps: The source first proves local finite presentation and zero-dimensional fibres via 38.11.2–38.11.3, then reduces around a point to a finite component in an elementary étale neighbourhood (37.41.6).
Flatness transports schematic density of U; the extraneous component is empty. The resulting finite locally free morphism has rank one on the dense open, hence everywhere after localization.
These local finite-presentation, fibre-dimension and étale-neighbourhood inputs remain individually named in G6. The generic-isomorphism hypothesis alone is not enough without flatness.

items.name: A proper generic isomorphism is dominated by a blowup
items.statement: Let S be qcqs and U⊂S quasi-compact open. Every proper X→S which is an isomorphism over U admits a factorization S′→X→S with S′→S a U-admissible blowup. Neither S nor X is required Noetherian.
proofSteps: First blow up an ideal of finite type defining the complement of U in S so that its inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor; then U is schematically dense.
Flatten the strict transform; flat-generic-isomorphism makes it an open subscheme of S′.
The strict transform is also proper over S′, so this open immersion is closed. Its image contains dense U; it is all of S′.
Compose the admissible blowups using 31.35.2. For S=Spec(A), U=D(p), finite generation and I[1/p]=A[1/p] imply p^N∈I for some N.

No flatness or Tor-independence is required to construct β; neither isomorphism nor almost isomorphism is asserted.

items.name: Transfer a retraction across a compatible comparison
items.statement: In any category, if u:A→M, v:M→N, and r:N→A satisfy r∘v∘u=id_A, then v followed by r is a retraction of u. In D(D), an almost retraction of D→RΓ(X_D,O) therefore composes with cohomology-base-change-map to split D→RΓ(X,O)⊗^L_R D almost. A further derived scalar extension preserves a supplied retraction.

proofSteps: Compose the supplied maps and use the unit triangle. Associativity proves the retraction identity; no conservativity, faithful flat descent or inverse of β is used.

For 6.1 first work over D=A∞⟨p^n/g⟩ and then apply −⊗^L_D D/p^m. Since p is regular on D, this is the displayed reduction of its unit; the left-hand derived scalar extension is already the object in the proof.

For 6.2 use the algebra map B→C to get Y_C→Y and a map RΓ(Y,O)→RΓ(Y_C,O). Compose the retraction to C with the almost retraction C→A from almost purity. The base change is along B, so no unproved A-flatness of B→C is required.

routes.brief: Extend the pending PerfectoidRamification brief from PAPER-ANDRE-18 with Bhatt's quantitative version. Import Perfectoid rings and spaces (PerfectoidSpaces) P0 almost-pro mathematics, P1 integral/tilted conventions, P2 rational root presentations and P3 almost purity; import generic derived completion and Koszul complexes from Derived de Rham cohomology (DerivedDeRhamCohomology) DD.1 and derived tensor/Hom from Enhanced derived sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves). Recover the inverse-limit Riemann extension only after the quantitative result, retaining lim-one. Do not infer arbitrary pointwise kernel vanishing from the final theorem without g-regularity. This strengthens the shared André ramification direction; it does not duplicate his completed integral-closure theorem or create a second perfectoidization. The continuation supplies the amplitude-zero cone proof of derived uniformity: c=p^k m survives tensor with arbitrary K, with g^(1/p^k) in m_t-almost modules and (tg)^(1/p^k) in ordinary modules. routes.brief: Build on Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra), importing its complete local coefficient and regular local homological algebra rather than recreating those foundations. The first final theorem is: every finite injective map A0→B0 of Noetherian commutative rings with A0 regular admits an A0-linear retraction. The second is: for every proper surjective f0:X0→Spec(A0) with A0 Noetherian regular, the unit A0→RΓ(X0,O_X0) splits in D(A0). Neither retraction is required to be multiplicative. Import PerfectoidSpaces P0–P3, PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra and Q3, the shared pending PerfectoidRamification quantitative tower theorem, DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1/E2, and the precise proper-coherent and formal-model suppliers requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations and AdicSpacesPartII R2. Construct the unramified and ramified regular local perfectoid covers separately, prove both positive Tor almost vanishing and detection of ordinary modules, and track the (!!) and star normalization steps. Prove the localization/completion, component, Cohen presentation and discriminant reductions, obstruction detection modulo p^m and its p²g-to-pg annihilator calculation, and almost vanishing on every annulus with its lim-one removal. For the derived theorem prove the perfectness of proper coherent cohomology, generic multisection reduction and corrected Proposition 6.2 with generic finite-étale SURJECTIVITY in mixed characteristic. Do not replace coherent base change by étale proper base change or ordinary base change without Tor control. Read the original equal-characteristic inputs and GR2 non-Noetherian domination theorem before closing the graph. Coordinate ownership of any splinter predicate with PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23's pending birational proposal; these statements can use explicit retractions and need no duplicate singularity vocabulary. Remark 5.5 is a question in this source, not a proved acceptance target. Continuation: proper H^0 integrality/localization/affinization are pinned library imports. Use the named SF.4 Stacks 0815–081T modification items and their R2 integral chart adapter. The bridge from ordinary proper base change needs only the E1 unit-compatible comparison morphism and composition of retractions, not its being an isomorphism. Finish the exact outstanding flattening leaves in G6; acquisition of GR2 alone does not close them.
